latest_release.name: v1.2.3
latest_release.body:
## 🏎️ Performance Improvements

## Faster runs and discovery with less memory

`run --all plan` takes up to 63% less time than in v1.2.2 and uses up to 18% less peak memory, measured at up to 1,000 units.

`find --dependencies` uses up to 89% less peak memory, measured at up to 5,000 units that share configuration through `include` and `read_terragrunt_config`, in the layout of [`BenchmarkDiscoverySharedConfig`](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_shared_config_test.go).

These numbers come from benchmarks on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, with a stand-in for `tofu` that exits immediately, so they time Terragrunt overhead alone.

## Faster dependent filters from below the repository root

A dependent filter, such as `--filter '...vpc'`, is faster when Terragrunt runs from a directory below the repository root. Terragrunt searched the rest of the repository once for the target and again for each dependent it found, so the time grew with the square of the number of dependents. It now searches once.

Finding every dependent of a unit from that unit's directory takes up to 99% less time than in v1.2.2, measured at up to 1,000 units. The same filter from the repository root takes up to 26% less time.

These numbers come from [benchmarks](https://github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/blob/main/internal/discovery/benchmark_dependents_test.go) on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395.

## Commands that never run OpenTofu/Terraform stop probing its version

Every command ran `tofu -version` at startup to set up provider caching, including the ones that never run OpenTofu/Terraform. These commands now skip that probe:

- `find`
- `list`
- `browse`
- `dag graph`
- `hcl fmt`
- `hcl validate`
- `catalog`
- `scaffold`
- `info strict`
- `stack clean`

They take up to 49% less time than in v1.2.2, measured at 100 units with OpenTofu 1.13.2 on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395:

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `terragrunt find` | 43.0 ms | 21.6 ms |
| `terragrunt list` | 37.5 ms | 20.6 ms |
| `terragrunt hcl fmt --check` | 39.3 ms | 21.2 ms |

## 🔒 Strict Controls Added

## `use-partial-parse-config-cache` strict control

The `--use-partial-parse-config-cache` flag, and its `TG_USE_PARTIAL_PARSE_CONFIG_CACHE` environment variable, has no effect, because Terragrunt no longer has a partial parse cache. The flag is deprecated, and Terragrunt warns when it is set:

```text
WARN  The `--use-partial-parse-config-cache` flag is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of Terragrunt. Terragrunt no longer has a partial parse cache for it to enable, so this flag has no effect.
```

Remove the flag from your commands. With the new [`use-partial-parse-config-cache`](https://docs.terragrunt.com/reference/strict-controls/active#use-partial-parse-config-cache) strict control enabled, passing it is an error instead:

```bash
terragrunt run --all --use-partial-parse-config-cache --strict-control use-partial-parse-config-cache -- plan
```

## 🔒 Strict Controls Updated

## `cas-source-inside-stack` warnings point at the source

The [`cas-source-inside-stack`](https://docs.terragrunt.com/reference/strict-controls/active#cas-source-inside-stack) warning named the `unit` or `stack` block and its source in one line:

```text
WARN  stack bar: unit "foo" in terragrunt.stack.hcl sets update_source_with_cas on source "./units/foo" inside the stack directory, so the generated stack also contains a copy of it; move the source out of the stack directory and select the stack with a // subdirectory in its source
```

Terragrunt now renders each warning as a diagnostic that shows the `source` attribute in the stack file:

```text
WARN   Source inside the stack directory
 --> ../catalog/terragrunt.stack.hcl:2:28
  |
2 |   source                 = "./units/foo"
  |                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = Stack generation copies the directory of this

# Terragrunt

[![Maintained by Gruntwork.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/maintained%20by-gruntwork.io-%235849a6.svg)](https://gruntwork.io/?ref=repo_terragrunt)
[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)
[![GoDoc](https://godoc.org/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt)
![OpenTofu Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/tofu-%3E%3D1.6.0-blue.svg)
![Terraform Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/tf-%3E%3D0.12.0-blue.svg)

Terragrunt is a flexible orchestration tool that allows Infrastructure as Code written in [OpenTofu](https://opentofu.org)/[Terraform](https://www.terraform.io) to scale.

Please see the following for more info, including install instructions and complete documentation:

* [Terragrunt Website](https://terragrunt.com)
* [Getting started with Terragrunt](https://docs.terragrunt.com/getting-started/quick-start/)
* [Terragrunt Documentation](https://docs.terragrunt.com/)
* [Terragrunt Scale](https://docs.terragrunt.com/terragrunt-scale/)
* [Contributing to Terragrunt](https://docs.terragrunt.com/community/contributing)
* [Commercial Support](https://gruntwork.io/support/)

## Join the Discord!

Join [our community](https://discord.com/invite/YENaT9h8jh) for discussions, support, and contributions:
